evidence_items.explanation: GDPval provides evidence of useful professional-task capability and reports progress toward expert deliverable quality. It does not establish that agents can reliably take over the broader work of the referenced occupations.

Epoch's examination explains why professional-task benchmarks do not directly establish occupational replacement capability. This limits what can be inferred from benchmark success without treating actual layoffs as necessary.

The study tests workflows reconstructed from production sessions and finds completion gaps in the evaluated systems. These results neither prove permanent impossibility nor exclude stronger systems outside the study.

This is a material reported counterexample, but the same account says Keenan checks every interaction and describes substantial errors and ongoing intervention. It supplies no independent evaluation of replacement capability across the referenced occupational scope.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved demonstration establishes sustained replacement capability across the occupational scope of the warning.
The recruitment case lacks independent validation, measured output quality, and a reliable accounting of human work still required.
Benchmark studies cover particular systems and dates; they do not exhaust all capabilities available by October 28, 2026.
No finite record of current failures can establish the unbounded 'never' prediction.
